category: hosted Stremio addon, universal torrent/debrid scrapers with live-TV and catalog resources

free_tier.stated: Free and accountless, but the public instance answered an anonymous stream request with a single placeholder stream titled 'MediaFusion public rate-limit exceeded 🐢'. The manifest itself claims 'configurationRequired: false'.
free_tier.notes: The rate limit is enforced per caller and silently replaces results with one link to a video explaining the limit (https://elfhosted.com/assets/public-rate-limit-exceeded.mp4).

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: stream descriptors, not objects

retention.stated: not applicable: the public instance stores nothing for the caller

egress.terms: Not metered; no bandwidth figure published. Playback is direct from the debrid provider or the source site, not proxied on the free instance.

interface_detail: Stremio addon protocol: resources include catalog, stream (types movie, series, tv, events; idPrefixes tt, tmdb:, tvdb:, mal:, mf, dl) and meta. Contact address published as abuse@elfhosted.com.
tooling: no install; add the manifest URL to Stremio. Requires the client's own debrid key for cached playback, and a MediaFlow proxy for household-wide sharing on the paid tier.
chaining: The broadest scraper of the free hosted addons found - it carries catalogs and live events, not just streams - so it can stand alone as a Stremio front end without AIOStreams in front of it.

limits.value: per-caller public rate limit, enforced; the number is not published and the over-limit response is a single placeholder stream

limits_note: Because the over-limit response is a well-formed 200 with one stream, a client cannot tell a throttled instance from an empty result except by reading the title text.

identity_cost.detail: Nothing to install the addon. A debrid account is required for cached playback.

reliability_note: Throttling is the normal state, not an error: the first anonymous call returned the rate-limit placeholder. The vendor sells a private instance as the fix.
confidence_note: Manifest fetched (669 bytes, HTTP 200) and a stream call made and read. Not measured: a configured instance with a debrid key, and whether the public limit resets hourly or daily. Downgraded from measured: no probe record with status, bytes and digest exists.

evidence.proved: HTTP 200, 669 bytes: id 'stremio.addons.mediafusion|elfhosted', name 'MediaFusion | ElfHosted', resources catalog/stream/meta/events, contactEmail abuse@elfhosted.com
HTTP 200 with exactly one stream: name '[🐢] MediaFusion', title 'MediaFusion public rate-limit exceeded 🐢', url https://elfhosted.com/assets/public-rate-limit-exceeded.mp4
the paid escape: 'Your own private MediaFusion addon for Stremio, bundled with a MediaFlow Proxy so the whole household can stream from one debrid account', USD 9.00 / month

notes: This is the clearest evidence found that a free hosted endpoint can be alive and useless at the same time: HTTP 200, valid JSON, schema-correct streams, zero content. Any measurement that only checked status or manifest would have scored it as working.
